clues: This city sits in southern Spain. It lies on the right bank of a big river in the Iberian Peninsula.
Summers here are the hottest in Spain and in all of Europe. They are very dry, while mild winters bring frequent rain.
Rome ruled this place long ago. Then Muslims took it in the eighth century and made it their capital.
This city has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any place on Earth. It holds the world record, with four in all.
The famed Mezquita-Catedral here is a Moorish work. It was named a World Heritage Site in 1984 and is now a church.
